# BambooHR

Connect BambooHR and your people are kept in step with it: an account from their start date, deactivated — every session signed out — at the end of their last day, and each department a group your administrators can map to roles.

## In BambooHR

In the portal, open **Directory sync**, choose **Using an HR system?**, and pick **BambooHR**. Then, in BambooHR:

1. Create a dedicated BambooHR user for the integration, with an access level that can see every employee — active and inactive — and their work email, job, department, supervisor, hire and termination dates.
2. Sign in as that user, open the account menu (your name, top right) → API Keys, and choose Add New Key. Name it "Cbox ID" and copy the key; it is shown once.
3. Paste the key and your company subdomain: the part before .bamboohr.com in the address you sign in at.

## What to paste into the portal

| Field | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| **Company subdomain** | The part before .bamboohr.com in the address you sign in at. |
| **API key** (secret) | Created by the integration user under their profile → API Keys. Shown once. |

The portal checks these with BambooHR before anything is stored, and never shows a secret again.

## What happens next

- The first sync starts straight away and runs in the background; the portal shows how it went.
- After that, BambooHR is asked for what changed, about every hour, with a full sync at least once a day.
- A person whose termination date has passed loses access at the end of that day, even if their status has not been updated yet. People on leave keep their account.
- People who left before the connection was made, and people who have not started yet, get no account.
- A person with no work email, or whose email already belongs to an account that is not linked to this connection, is listed as not synced — by their BambooHR employee ID — and nobody else is held up.
- If a sync would suddenly deactivate more than half of your people, it deactivates nobody and says why: that is almost always permissions that changed in BambooHR, not a mass layoff.

BambooHR's own guide: <https://documentation.bamboohr.com/docs/getting-started>.
